close_reason: Doc-only fixes: updated stale/ambiguous rustdoc and CHANGELOG entries
description:
Trigger: pkix-revocation/CHANGELOG.md lines 22-24 (the 1.0.0 entry for the serde feature) says: 'pkix-revocation::DerError is now a re-export of pkix_path::DerError rather than an independent type with identical shape; pattern matches still work, constructions via the (formerly tuple) DerError(e) syntax now use DerError::new(e).'

Verifiable claim: 'pattern matches still work.'

Actual state: pkix_path::DerError is now `pub struct DerError { inner: Option<der::Error>, message: BoxStr }` with both fields private (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:130-148). External consumers cannot use ANY positional or named-field pattern. A consumer who previously wrote:

    if let Error::CrlParseError(DerError(_)) = err { ... }

now sees a hard compile error: 'expected tuple struct or tuple variant, found struct `DerError`.' The migration story in the CHANGELOG is wrong.

Bad behavior: a 1.0 consumer reading the migration notes will believe their pattern matches still compile, hit a compile error, and have to figure out the actual fix on their own.

Fix: rewrite the CHANGELOG sentence to:
'Pattern matches against the inner DerError tuple form no longer compile (DerError is now a struct with private fields, not a tuple struct). Match the outer Error::CrlParseError(_) variant instead, or bind by name and call Display: `if let Error::CrlParseError(e) = err { eprintln!("{e}"); }.`'

Tradeoff: this is pre-1.0 (0.x version is allowed to break things per AGENTS.md framing). The fix is purely documentation accuracy.
title: CHANGELOG: 'pattern matches still work' for DerError refactor is inaccurate
